slides.title: VT-MUSE: Multimodal Unified Sequential Visuotactile Representation Learning for Manipulation
slides.highlight: VT-MUSE introduces a framework for learning unified visuotactile representations that capture temporal evolution and cross-modal dependencies, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception.

card.one_liner: VT-MUSE learns unified sequential visuotactile representations to improve contact-rich robotic manipulation in simulation and real-world.
card.key_idea: A two-stage framework: Stage I aligns modalities via temporal consistency; Stage II uses a conditional variational model to reconstruct masked visual and tactile depth-flow sequences.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on UniVTAC simulation and physical robot tasks; outperformed strongest baselines by 16.25% (sim) and 63.75% (real) in success rates.
card.limitation: Uses fixed sample strides and limited pretraining task diversity (up to 7 tasks), requiring further scaling law validation.

slides.title: HiTac-WAM: A Hierarchical Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: HIERARCHICAL TACTILE WORLD ACTION MODEL FOR ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: HiTac-WAM forecasts future tactile states by factorizing contact state, 3D deformation, and slip risk into a directed hierarchy. This approach improves real-robot success rates in contact-rich tasks like chip grasping and USB insertion through tactile-guided action selection and corrective replanning.

card.one_liner: HiTac-WAM improves contact-rich manipulation by forecasting hierarchical tactile consequences to rank and verify action candidates.
card.key_idea: A world action model using a directed hierarchy (contact $\rightarrow$ deformation $\rightarrow$ slip risk) with stop-gradient conditioning and directed attention to predict tactile outcomes for candidate action chunks.
card.evaluation: Tested on chip grasping, blackboard erasing, and USB insertion. Success rate rose from 31.1% (baseline) to 72.2% (full system) across 360 real-robot trials.
card.limitation: Forecast quality on model-generated action chunks was not evaluated separately, and predicted slip risk is not calibrated for online detection.

slides.title: The Missing Touch: Spatially Distributed Tactile Feedback Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that spatially distributed tactile feedback reduces the gap between teleoperated and natural human trajectories, supporting MOSAIC's focus on force-based skill acquisition and human-AI alignment.

card.one_liner: Spatially distributed tactile feedback makes teleoperated robot movements more natural, consistent, and human-like.
card.key_idea: A 32-DoF cutaneous shape display reproduces localized deformations from a vision-based tactile sensor, complementing kinesthetic force feedback to reduce corrective movements.
card.evaluation: Tested 10-12 participants on button discrimination and peg-rolling tasks; used Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) to compare teleoperated vs. natural trajectories.
card.limitation: Evaluated using only a 2-DoF system and two specific tasks; may not generalize to higher-DoF dexterous manipulation.

slides.title: ViHaTeleop: A Low-Cost, Lightweight Visual-Haptic Teleoperation System for Dexterous Manipulation Learning
slides.highlight: This system utilizes vibrotactile feedback and multi-modal demonstration collection to improve success rates in contact-critical tasks, supporting the MOSAIC goal of estimating procedural and tacit skills through ego-exo views and force-based feedback.

card.one_liner: ViHaTeleop is a low-cost, lightweight visual-haptic system improving success rates in contact-critical dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines SLAM-based wrist tracking, fisheye hand tracking, and LRA vibrotactile feedback with a tactile-aware retargeting constraint to ensure parallel fingertip alignment for better sensor engagement.
card.evaluation: User study (n=9) across six tasks; haptics improved success rates (+2.2 to +15.6%). Visual-tactile policies showed +8% average success over vision-only.
card.limitation: Small user sample size (n=9), lack of external ground-truth tracking benchmarks, and limited training data for imitation learning.

slides.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces SoftVTBench, a dataset pairing multi-view RGB and tactile data with physical ground truth to evaluate interaction quality. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception of hybrid states and physical interactions.

card.one_liner: A visuo-tactile dataset and benchmark for evaluating both task success and physical interaction quality in deformable-object manipulation.
card.key_idea: Introduces SoftVTBench with 4,000 demonstrations and a Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR) using hidden FEM states to penalize excessive object compression.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Diffusion Policy, π0.5, and FastWAM on in-distribution and OOD sets; results show TSR often masks physical interaction failures.
card.limitation: The deformation tolerance is an operational simulation criterion, not a real-world material-failure or damage threshold.

slides.title: Koala Gripper: Co-designing Robotic Grippers and Data-Capture Devices for Scaling Dexterous Manipulation Learning
slides.tldr: CO-DESIGNED GRIPPER FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION LEARNING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a co-design framework for data capture and robotic execution devices to improve dexterity and grasp capability, supporting the MOSAIC goal of enhancing skill acquisition through learning from demonstration.

card.one_liner: A co-designed robotic gripper and data-capture system for scaling dexterous manipulation via imitation learning.
card.key_idea: Simultaneous design of a handheld capture device and robot gripper featuring a 3-DoF morphology, underactuated linkage fingers, and a monolithic dual-thumb for versatile grasping.
card.evaluation: Validated via force-parity tests, qualitative grasping of diverse objects, and diffusion-policy execution on a Franka Emika FR3 using handheld and teleoperated data.
card.limitation: Lacks thumb adduction for in-hand re-orientation and force-state information in collected data for force-reactive policies.

slides.title: Don't Drop the BATON: Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation via Agentic Subtask Exploration and Transition-aware Memory
slides.tldr: AGENTIC SUBTASK EXPLORATION FOR LONG-HORIZON ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: BATON utilizes agentic subtask exploration and transition-aware memory to decompose long-horizon tasks, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt at test time and self-monitor via verifier agents.

card.one_liner: Baton enables long-horizon robot manipulation by exploring subtasks individually and managing transitions via language memory.
card.key_idea: An LLM agent orchestrates a frozen VLA using hierarchical subtask exploration (additive cost) and transition-aware memory (invocation, handoff, and lookahead transitions) to ensure seamless subtask composition.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on RoboMemArena thousand-step tasks; improved task success rate by 11.6% and cumulative success rate by 14.9% over the current state-of-the-art.

slides.title: ForeTime-VLA: Causal Future-Token Distillation from a World Action Model for Conveyor-Belt Manipulation
slides.tldr: CAUSAL FUTURE-TOKEN DISTILLATION FOR DYNAMIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: ForeTime-VLA improves conveyor-belt manipulation by distilling future-aware representations from a world action model into a causal policy. This approach enhances grasp success rates for moving objects without the deployment cost of a full world model.

card.one_liner: ForeTime-VLA improves dynamic conveyor-belt manipulation by distilling future-aware representations from a world action model.
card.key_idea: A causal history encoder predicts a 64-D action-equivalent future code, manipulation phase, and transition horizon to condition a $\pi_{0.5}$ VLA policy via dual-path injection.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a conveyor-belt dataset and real robots; achieved 81.1% stationary and 58.9% slow-moving grasp success, outperforming $\pi_{0.5}$ and other VLA baselines.
card.limitation: Currently limited to one conveyor-belt embodiment and an offline teacher derived from a fixed video backbone.
